items.excerpt: Indie dev Tomas Sala accuses a studio of using AI to clone his viral potato-peeling game, saying the copy was churned out with generative tools while he refuses to let 'a cheap copy win.'

Microsoft has filed a patent for a machine learning system that trains on a player's session data to predict the moments they'll be least irritated by in-game ads, turning player behaviour models into ad-placement tooling.

An opinion piece from the Tokyo Game Show 2026 floor: nostalgia-heavy line-ups sat alongside an AI-forward show agenda, with Japanese studios openly debating how far generative tools should go in production.
A Tokyo Game Show 2026 report finds more than 85% of surveyed Japanese game developers now use generative AI somewhere in production, with adoption concentrated in art, prototyping and text.
A Chinese court awarded MiHoYo $112,000 after an AI voice service cloned Genshin Impact character voices, one of the first game-industry rulings on synthetic voice likeness.
Microsoft published a draft code of practice for AI training data and invited public feedback, a document that would set ground rules for how artists' and studios' work can be used to train models.
Level-5's CEO admits the studio used generative AI to make its digital showcase 'more spectacular', apologising after fans spotted AI imagery in the Professor Layton and Yo-kai Watch presentation.
Hundreds of unionised Blizzard workers ratified a contract that gives them a formal say in how generative AI is adopted at the studio, alongside layoff protections.
